focus: v1 user migration simulation per agent; ADR-0011 detect table vs real v1 footprint; step order; npm-global users

findings.claim: v1 checks npm `latest` every hour, and nothing new will be published there, so v1 users get no "outdated" warning.
findings.evidence: src/cli.ts:384-399 defines fetchLatestVersion(), called only at src/cli.ts:1151 (inside the `ctx_doctor` command) and src/cli.ts:1302/1320 (inside `/ctx-upgrade`). Both are user-triggered CLI commands. No cron, no setInterval, no SessionStart hook, and no other caller of fetchLatestVersion exists anywhere in src/ or hooks/ (checked with grep across the full v1 tree). There is no hourly timer at all.
findings.note: The doc's bottom-line claim (v1 users get no outdated warning once npm publishing stops) is still correct, but for a different reason: the check only runs when the user manually runs doctor/upgrade, not on a background hourly cadence. The doc should say 'v1 only checks npm latest when the user runs ctx_doctor or /ctx-upgrade' so a reader does not assume an automatic background notice exists.
findings.fix: Replace the 'every hour' sentence in ADR-0011 with: 'v1 only checks npm `latest` when the user runs `ctx_doctor` or `/ctx-upgrade` (src/cli.ts:1151, 1302) — there is no background/periodic check.'
findings.archaeology: N/A — not a regression, a doc inaccuracy. fetchLatestVersion has had exactly these two call sites since it was introduced; no historical hourly-check code was found or removed.

findings.claim: The v1-migration E2E case set (ADR-0017 R8) runs 'a temp HOME with a real v1 install per agent -> v2 install -> /ctx-upgrade -> doctor clean -> a routing case passes', intended to prove no v1 user is left broken.
findings.evidence: Confirmed by source inspection that Copilot CLI and VS Code Copilot v1 hooks dispatch through the bare global binary name, not an absolute path: src/adapters/copilot-cli/hooks.ts:77 returns `context-mode hook copilot-cli ${scriptName}`; src/adapters/vscode-copilot/hooks.ts:114 returns `context-mode hook vscode-copilot ${hookType.toLowerCase()}`. This matches what ADR-0011 already states (global-bin dependency), confirmed by git archaeology: introduced in 9f34c6f1 ('Add GitHub Copilot CLI + Antigravity CLI (agy) support (#787)'), commit message explicitly documents the global-binary dispatch as deliberate design, not a bug. No contradiction found here against the doc.
findings.gap: R8's case set description does not state whether the migration E2E actually simulates an npm-global install (`npm install -g context-mode`) for the Copilot CLI / VS Code agents specifically, which are the two hosts ADR-0011 names as broken mid-migration. Without that, the exact 3-step order (install v2 -> /ctx-upgrade -> npm uninstall -g) that R3 claims closes the gap is asserted but not shown to be exercised by a case.
findings.fix: Name the npm-global + Copilot-CLI/VS-Code case explicitly in ADR-0017 R8 (or in the e2e/live/cases file list) so the order claim in R3 has a concrete, citable test, not just a narrative.
findings.archaeology: git log -S for the hook builders in both adapters shows a single introducing commit each (9f34c6f1 for copilot-cli; same PR for vscode-copilot), no later commit changed the global-bin dispatch, so the risk window described in ADR-0011/ADR-0017 is real and has existed unchanged since v1 added these adapters.

no_new_findings_on: ADR-0011 cache-heal hook naming (hooks/context-mode-cache-heal.{mjs,sh}) — verified against start.mjs:314-385 (globalHooksDir/context-mode-cache-heal.mjs + legacy .sh cleanup): matches the doc exactly.

ADR-0017 R3 upgrade order (install v2 -> /ctx-upgrade -> npm uninstall -g last) — already the settled r3 fix for the ordering bug flagged in REVIEW-r2.md:156 and BOTTLENECKS-r3.md:72; not re-flagged since the doc already reflects the corrected order.
